entries.definition: fairness that takes different needs and barriers into account
entries.translation: عدالت با توجه به نیازهای متفاوت
entries.example: Equity may require different kinds of support for different learners.

entries.definition: equal rights, status, or opportunities for people
entries.example: The discussion connected equality with fair access to public services.

entries.definition: the presence of different backgrounds or characteristics within a group
entries.example: The library’s collection reflects the diversity of the neighborhood.

entries.definition: making it possible for people to participate and belong
entries.example: Inclusion requires more than inviting people to a room they cannot enter.

entries.definition: being prevented from joining or accessing a group or activity
entries.example: The report describes exclusion caused by inaccessible registration forms.

entries.definition: how easily people with different needs can use a place or service
entries.example: The renovation improved accessibility without removing the old building’s character.

entries.definition: unfair treatment based on a person’s group or characteristics
entries.example: The policy explains how to report discrimination at work.

entries.definition: an unfair opinion formed without adequate knowledge of a person or group
entries.example: Meeting people as individuals can challenge prejudice.

entries.definition: an oversimplified belief about everyone in a group
entries.example: The story questions a stereotype rather than repeating it as a fact.

entries.definition: an unfair difference in access, status, or resources
entries.example: The study examines inequality in access to transport.

entries.definition: not having enough resources to meet basic living needs
entries.example: The project listens to people affected by poverty before proposing support.

entries.definition: a condition of economic success and improved living standards
entries.example: The plan asks how local prosperity can benefit more residents.

entries.definition: organized support for people who need help with basic living needs
entries.example: The guide explains how residents can ask about welfare services.

entries.definition: services intended to maintain or improve people’s health
entries.example: Reliable transportation can influence access to healthcare.

entries.definition: homes considered as a supply or public need
entries.example: The council discussed housing near schools and workplaces.

entries.definition: movement from one place to live in another
entries.example: The exhibition explores migration through individual family stories.

entries.definition: coming into a country to live there
entries.example: The museum describes immigration from the receiving country’s perspective.

entries.definition: leaving a country to live in another
entries.example: The letter explains the family’s reasons for emigration.

entries.definition: participation in a wider community while building connections within it
entries.example: Language classes can support integration without requiring people to abandon their heritage.

entries.definition: legal membership of a country and the rights and duties connected with it
entries.example: The lesson distinguishes citizenship from temporary residence.

entries.definition: the systems and practices used to direct an organization or community
entries.example: Good governance includes clear responsibilities and ways to question decisions.

entries.definition: an agreed set of principles guiding decisions and actions
entries.example: The policy explains how the library handles private information.

entries.definition: laws considered or adopted by a law-making body
entries.example: The article explains the purpose of the proposed legislation.

entries.definition: an official rule controlling a particular activity
entries.example: The regulation sets safety requirements for the public building.

entries.definition: action taken to make sure a rule or law is followed
entries.example: Fair enforcement requires clear rules and consistent procedures.

entries.definition: fair treatment through principles, institutions, or decisions
entries.example: The discussion considered access to justice as well as written rights.

entries.definition: a system in which people influence government through participation and representation
entries.example: The lesson examines how participation and accountability relate to democracy.

entries.definition: taking an active part in an activity or decision
entries.example: Public participation helped planners notice routes missing from the map.

entries.definition: speaking or acting on behalf of a person or group
entries.example: The committee reviewed whether its membership provided fair representation.

entries.definition: openness about information and how decisions are made
entries.example: Publishing the selection criteria improved transparency.

entries.definition: the duty to explain decisions and accept responsibility for them
entries.example: The project needs accountability as well as a clear budget.

entries.definition: misuse of entrusted power for improper personal gain
entries.example: The procedure separates roles to reduce opportunities for corruption.

entries.definition: organized support for a cause or for people’s needs
entries.example: Her advocacy focused on making the station usable for more passengers.

entries.definition: organized action intended to bring social or political change
entries.example: The exhibition compares different forms of peaceful activism.

entries.definition: support based on shared interests or concern for others
entries.example: The volunteers showed solidarity with families affected by the closure.

entries.definition: the strength of connections holding a group together
entries.example: Shared projects can contribute to social cohesion.

entries.definition: a feeling of being disconnected from a group or surroundings
entries.example: The unfamiliar procedures increased her sense of alienation.

entries.definition: the process of pushing people away from full participation or influence
entries.example: The report examines marginalization without blaming those excluded.

entries.definition: an advantage available to some people but not to others
entries.example: The discussion asked how an unnoticed privilege can shape daily choices.

entries.definition: the worth of a person and the respect they deserve
entries.example: The service aims to offer help while protecting each person’s dignity.

entries.definition: traditions, places, and knowledge passed from earlier generations
entries.example: The exhibition presents heritage as something people use and reinterpret.

entries.definition: including several cultural backgrounds or traditions
entries.example: The multicultural festival gave each group space to explain its contribution.

entries.definition: involving communication or relationships between cultures
entries.example: The exchange encouraged intercultural understanding through ordinary conversation.

entries.definition: relating to the characteristics of a population
entries.example: The demographic information helped planners identify who was missing from the survey.

entries.definition: people born and living during a broadly similar period
entries.example: Each generation added its own memories to the family collection.

entries.definition: to live or function alongside others at the same time
entries.example: Different uses of the park can coexist with thoughtful planning.

entries.definition: felt or done by each person toward the other
entries.example: The partnership depends on mutual respect rather than identical opinions.

entries.definition: involving a group acting or deciding together
entries.example: The garden was a collective effort across several streets.

entries.definition: relating to participation and responsibilities in community life
entries.example: The class practiced civic discussion by examining a local planning question.

entries.definition: organized by ordinary members of a community rather than its senior leaders
entries.example: The grassroots project began with neighbors sharing tools.
